name: Wu Caiping
current_role: Individual top-10 shareholder (~2.6%) of Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology (CVTE, SZSE: 002841)
profile: Wu Caiping (吴彩平) is a long-standing individual shareholder of CVTE (Shiyuan Electronic), the Guangzhou maker of interactive flat panels, display control boards and the Seewo/MAXHUB brands, listed in Shenzhen in 2017. Wealth comes from that stake (~18.3m shares, ~2.6% as of Sept 2026). Not part of the founders' concerted-action group and holds no disclosed executive role; otherwise very low profile.
interesting_fact: Ranked among CVTE's top 10 shareholders in the 2024 annual report alongside founders Huang Zhengcong, Wang Yiran and Sun Yonghui; CVTE, founded in 2005, is one of the world's largest suppliers of LCD TV main control boards and interactive whiteboards.
notes: Very private passive shareholder; no public interviews found. Only route is CVTE's board-secretary/IR office (email is company IR, not personal). Gender and age not confirmed.

name: Ye Dalin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering Co., Ltd. (SZSE ChiNext: 300813)
profile: Ye Dalin (叶大林, b. 1960) founded Hangzhou-based Tailin Bioengineering, which makes sterility-testing, microbial-detection, filtration and isolator equipment for pharma and biotech labs. He and his wife Ni Weiju are the controlling shareholders (~57%), and the company listed on ChiNext in 2020. In 2026 Tailin was pursuing a convertible-bond issue to fund high-performance filter and functional-membrane production.
interesting_fact: Tailin's core products are sterility-test pumps and microbial-limit testers used by drug makers, and its 2026 fundraising targets industrialising high-performance filters and functional membranes.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 13 years as a lab technician: at Zhejiang Hospital (1981-88) and the Hangzhou Central Blood Station (1988-94), then ran the Zhejiang Pan'an Kaixuan microporous filter factory (1994-99) before founding Hangzhou Tailin Industrial in 1999.
notes: Low media profile; best route is the company board-secretary office. Wealth shared with wife Ni Weiju.

name: Wang Yaofang
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Changzhou Qianhong Bio-Pharma (SZSE: 002550); controlling shareholder (~20%)
profile: Wang Yaofang (王耀方, b. 1953), a senior engineer and licensed pharmacist, rose from deputy director of the state-owned Changzhou Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory to lead its restructured successor, Qianhong Bio-Pharma, a heparin API and enzyme-drug maker he took public in Shenzhen in 2011. Qianhong is now pushing original drugs such as QHRD106 and QHRD107 through clinical trials.
interesting_fact: Qianhong is one of China's main exporters of heparin sodium API (made from pig intestinal mucosa) and also sells pancreatic kininogenase; at a May 2026 earnings call Wang said its novel drugs QHRD106 (Phase IIb) and QHRD107 (Phase IIa) were on schedule.
deep_cut_fact: He began at the state-run Changzhou Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory, rising to deputy factory director, before leading its spin-out Changzhou Biochemical Qianhong Pharmaceutical as chairman and GM; he holds three professional titles: senior engineer, national licensed pharmacist and senior economist.
notes: Since the 2024 annual report the company's legal representative is Wang Ke (acts in concert with Wang Yaofang); confirm current chairman title before outreach. Best route: board secretary office.

name: Hugh Osmond
current_role: Founder, Sun Capital Partners (2001) and Osmond Capital (2017); Non-Executive Director, Coppa Collective plc (formerly Various Eateries, AIM)
profile: Hugh Osmond (b. 1962), an Oxford-educated former medic, co-led the 1993 PizzaExpress flotation with Luke Johnson, founded pub group Punch Taverns in 1997 and co-founded closed-life-fund consolidator Pearl Group (bought from Henderson for GBP1.1bn in 2005). He now invests via Sun Capital and Osmond Capital, bought Capital Physio in 2019, and founded Coppa Club operator Various Eateries in 2014.
interesting_fact: Read medicine at Merton College, Oxford, but went into hospitality; he spotted in early-1990s America how many places served a decent meal for $5-10, which convinced him and Luke Johnson that PizzaExpress could become a national chain.
deep_cut_fact: He started running clubs and bars while at university, ran clubs in America after graduating in 1983, and admits to a brief stint trying to run a computer company ('I don't know what possessed me') before working at a small Madrid investment bank.

public_contacts.value: Alma PR (Coppa Collective's PR adviser), 71-73 Carter Lane, London EC4V 5EQ

notes: Significant Conservative Party donor. No personal social accounts found; best route is via Coppa Collective's PR (Alma PR) or Osmond Capital.

name: Wang Jianhua
current_role: Director and Chief Technology Officer, Qingdao Topscomm Communication Inc. (SSE: 603421); chairman 2012-May 2025
profile: Wang Jianhua (王建华, b. 1966), a senior engineer with a postgraduate degree, co-founded Qingdao Topscomm with Zeng Fanyi in 2008. Topscomm makes power-line carrier communication chips and modules, smart-meter and grid-automation equipment sold largely to China's State Grid, and listed in Shanghai in 2016. He chaired the company until May 2025 (succeeded by Liu Min) and remains a director, CTO and a major shareholder (~91.6m shares).
interesting_fact: Topscomm is a grid-edge tech play: it designs its own power-line carrier (PLC) communication chips used in electricity-meter reading networks, and its business scope now spans energy storage, EV charging and PV equipment.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a founder-chairman, he doubled as the company's hands-on technologist: CTO since 2015 and, from 2019 to 2024, head of Topscomm's in-house Chip and Basic Theory Research Institute; he also runs its fire-safety subsidiary Dingxin Xiaofang.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/grid-tech episode (PLC chips for smart grid). Low media profile; route via Topscomm securities office.

name: Sharon Harel
current_role: Founder, WestEnd Films (London film/TV production, financing and international sales company)
profile: Sharon Harel-Cohen is a London-based film producer and financier who has produced or financed 50+ films, chiefly through Capitol Films, which she co-founded in 1989 and sold in 2006 (Gosford Park, Spider, Death and the Maiden). In 2008 she launched WestEnd Films with Eve Schoukroun and Maya Amsellem; its credits include HBO's Valley of Tears. Her listed wealth is shared with her husband, private-equity and impact-investing pioneer Sir Ronald Cohen.
interesting_fact: Executive producer on Robert Altman's Gosford Park, Polanski's Death and the Maiden and the Oscar-nominated Albert Nobbs; she received the Olswang Business Award from Carlton Women in Film and Television in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: She began as a producer in Israel on the classic Halahaka ('The Troupe'), which she co-wrote, then produced Tom Hanks' 1986 Tri-Star film Every Time We Say Goodbye; her degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem is in Chinese Studies and Western Philosophy.
notes: Also known as Sharon Harel-Cohen / Lady Cohen. Best route is WestEnd Films general inbox. Husband Sir Ronald Cohen (Apax founder, impact investing) may be the more relevant podcast guest.

name: Charles W Scharf
current_role: Chairman (since Oct 2025) and CEO (since Oct 2019), Wells Fargo & Company; Director, Microsoft
profile: Charlie Scharf (b. 1965) is a career banker who rose under Jamie Dimon from Commercial Credit through Salomon Smith Barney, Citigroup, Bank One and JPMorgan Chase, where he ran retail and integrated Washington Mutual in 2008. He was CEO of Visa (2012-16) and BNY Mellon (2017-19) before taking over Wells Fargo in 2019 to work through its regulatory consent orders; he became chairman in 2025 and sits on Microsoft's board.
interesting_fact: Jamie Dimon hired him in 1987 for a back-office job at Commercial Credit; within six months he was Dimon's assistant, and he spent some 25 years working alongside Dimon before becoming a rival bank CEO.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a stockbroker, he grew up in Westfield, New Jersey, and as a teenager worked back-office jobs at Manhattan brokerage firms; he earned his NYU Stern MBA at night (executive programme, 1991) while already working for Dimon.
notes: Highly visible Fortune-100 CEO; requests go via Wells Fargo corporate communications (newsroom.wf.com). Microsoft board seat is relevant to a data-center angle.
